chunks: With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Hasan ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn A'idh, from Ibn Salama - and he is Abu Khadija, and his name is Salem ibn Makram, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Blood-letting on the head is performed by a shibr from the tip of the nose and a fitr between the eyebrows. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) used to call it the saving. In another narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) used to perform blood-letting on his head and name it as the refuging or the saving.
ai.seo_question: Where exactly on the head should cupping be performed according to the Prophet's tradition?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to establish the Sunnah of cupping at the 'Manqidha' point (between the eyebrows), a practice attributed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) as a means of physical purification and spiritual protection. The terminology 'Al-Munqidha' (the Savior) and 'Al-Mughitha' (the Helper) underscores the Shia scholarly view of this procedure as both a medicinal remedy and a form of seeking divine aid against ailments.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from Hasan bin Ali, from Ahmad bin ‘A’idh, from Ibn Salama, and he is Abu Khadija, and his name is Salem bin Makram, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:

Blood-letting on the head is performed by a shibr [1] from the tip of the nose (vertically) and a fitr [2] between the eyebrows. The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, used to call it the saving. In another narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, used to perform blood-letting on his head and name it as the refuging or the saving.
